I found an article that I thought /v/tv would enjoy. It was about stephen hawking finding the 'genius' in normal people. when i tried to search 'tv' in the default search it said I needed to input at least 3 characters. Searching 'tv' (2 chars) may still be relevant. Just a thought.

MySQL doesn't like that, and I suspect if Voat uses a different db, that wouldn't like it either. Basically it would require an index pointing from all 2-char possible strings to the records where they exist. Building, maintaining, and searching that index would take a bunch of computing resources.

From the MySQL manual (emphasis mine):

The minimum and maximum lengths of words to be indexed are defined by the ft_min_word_len and ft_max_word_len system variables. The >default minimum value is four characters; the default maximum is version dependent. If you change either value, you must rebuild your >FULLTEXT indexes.

http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/fulltext-fine-tuning.html

I saw The Matrix when it first came out in theaters. The ad campaign for it was terrible in my opinion and so I wasn't expecting much. It was just "What is The Matrix?" with Keanu Reeves dodging bullets in slow motion. That's it. I was expecting the movie to fail to live up to the vague hype the ads were trying so hard to build up around it. I was pleasantly surprised. Back then, nobody had ever done a movie quite like that. In terms of special effects it was revolutionary, and its use of the allegory of the cave type of story hadn't been done that way before in pop culture. As a result, it's all anyone could talk about for the next few years. Everything was saturated with it until the two sequels pretty much ruined it...

Also, Dark City. I saw that when it came out in theaters and was blown away by it too. It remains one of my favorite movies of all time. I think it holds up really well to the test of time and will continue to do so in the future.
